terms.meaning: A named color such as primary or background that points to a shade in the palette.
A link inside the token file that points to another value, written in curly braces.
A plain text table where each line is a row and commas separate the columns.
A transparent color layer placed over an image so text stays readable.

depends_on: the design system data file slide-backgrounds.csv
Python standard library modules json, csv, re, sys, and pathlib

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: File setup and file locations
sections.what: Describes the script as a fetcher for slide background images, then sets the project root and the locations of the token file and the background CSV file, both found relative to the script.
sections.why: Likely reason: the locations are calculated from the script's own position so the paths work from any folder.
sections.watch_out: The project root is found by going up five folder levels from the script, so moving the script breaks every path.

sections.name: resolve_token_reference
sections.title: Turning a token link into a value
sections.what: If a value is written as a token link in curly braces, follows the path through the token file and returns the actual value. If the value is not a link, it is returned unchanged.
sections.why: Semantic colors point to palette shades, so links must be resolved before the colors can be used.
sections.watch_out: A broken link returns nothing, and the caller must handle that empty result.

sections.name: load_brand_colors (part 1)
sections.title: Loading brand colors from semantic tokens
sections.what: Reads the token file and tries the semantic primary, secondary, accent, and background colors first, resolving each link. If the main colors are present, it returns them. Otherwise it searches the palette by known color names.
sections.why: Likely reason: prefers the named semantic colors and falls back to palette names from an older naming scheme.
sections.watch_out: If only one of the two main semantic colors is present, the function silently moves to the fallback search.

sections.name: load_brand_colors (part 2)
sections.title: Filling defaults for brand colors
sections.what: Finishes the fallback path by using the palette names it found, or built-in defaults for any missing color. The background comes from the dark palette's 800 shade when present. If the file is missing or malformed, it returns the full set of defaults.
sections.why: Likely reason: the slides still get usable colors when the token file is incomplete or absent.
sections.watch_out: The defaults are fixed hex colors, so a missing token file produces a plausible-looking but off-brand result without any warning.

sections.name: load_backgrounds_config
sections.title: Loading background settings from the CSV
sections.what: Reads the background CSV and returns a lookup where each row is keyed by its slide type. If the file is missing, it prints a warning and returns an empty lookup.
sections.why: Lets each slide type have its own background settings, edited in one file.
sections.watch_out: A slide type with no matching row gets nothing, so the caller must check for it.

sections.name: get_overlay_css
sections.title: Dark overlay style builder
sections.what: Creates the CSS for a layer placed over a background photo so text stays readable. It picks one of several named styles and builds the color from brand colors. An unknown style name silently uses the default dark gradient.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps text readable on busy photos while using brand colors.
sections.watch_out: Two of the overlay styles use fixed dark colors instead of brand colors, so they will not follow a brand change.

sections.name: get_curated_images
sections.title: Preselected photo list lookup
sections.what: Returns the list of built-in photo links for a slide type. Unknown slide types get the hero photos instead of an error.
sections.why: Likely reason: the code notes say the photos are chosen in advance so no photo service is needed.
sections.watch_out: A typo in a slide type quietly returns hero photos, so the wrong image can appear without any warning.

sections.name: get_pexels_search_url
sections.title: Pexels search link builder
sections.what: Builds a web address that opens a Pexels photo search for the given keywords, so a person can choose a photo by hand.
sections.why: Used as a fallback when no preselected photo exists for a slide type.

sections.name: get_background_image
sections.title: Main photo lookup for a slide
sections.what: Loads brand colors and per-slide settings, then returns the first preselected photo with its overlay, credit line and search link. If no photos exist for the slide type, it returns no photo address and a search link instead.
sections.why: The code notes that photos are preselected, so nothing is fetched live from the internet.
sections.watch_out: In the fallback case the url value is empty, so any caller must check it before using it.

sections.name: generate_css_for_background
sections.title: Background slide style writer
sections.what: Writes the CSS rules that place the photo behind a slide, cover the area, add the overlay, and keep content above it. If there is no photo, it writes only a comment with a search link.
sections.why: Keeps the slide background setup in one place so each slide looks consistent.
sections.watch_out: The photo address is placed into the CSS without escaping, so an address containing a quote mark could break the style.

sections.name: main
sections.title: Command-line options and output
sections.what: Runs when the file is called from a terminal. It can print brand colors, list slide types, or print the photo as plain text, CSS, JSON, or a list of all links, depending on the flags given.
sections.why: Lets a person or another script get a background without writing Python code.
sections.watch_out: The JSON output uses the json module, and the import of it is in the file header, which was not visible. If that import is missing, the JSON option will crash.

sections.name: entry point
sections.title: Start-up guard
sections.what: Runs the command-line main function only when this file is started directly, not when another file imports it.
sections.why: Standard Python pattern so the file can be reused as a library.

summary: Helps pick slide background settings by reading brand colors from the design token file and background options from a CSV file. Only five of its twelve sections were included in this packet, so the image-fetching steps are unclear here.
purpose: Supplies the colors and background choices that slide backgrounds and their color overlays need.
why: Likely reason: keeps backgrounds in step with the brand colors and lets background choices be edited in a spreadsheet-style file.
how: The script reads the token file and resolves linked color references into actual values, with a fallback set of defaults. It reads the background CSV into a lookup keyed by slide type. The header says the full script fetches Pexels images without an API key, but those steps are not in this packet.
inputs: The assets/design-tokens.json file and the slide-backgrounds.csv file in the design system data folder.
outputs: A set of primary, secondary, accent, and background colors, and a lookup of background settings by slide type. The packet does not show what the rest of the script returns.
risks: If the token file is missing or broken, the script silently uses built-in default colors that may not match the brand. Its location calculation depends on the script staying in its current folder.
debug: If colors look wrong, check the token file for the semantic color entries and confirm the defaults are not being used. If a slide type has no background, check the CSV for a matching slide type row. A warning line means the CSV was not found.
